title: Contract case
description: One case of the shared L2 corpus (contract/cases/): a public call and its inputs, how far it runs, and the reference's outcome. The Python runner (contract/runners/run_python.py) makes the public calls; the pure-Rust host (sdm-contract-run) starts the core operations under `core`. A case taken from the Phase 1b inventory keeps every key the inventory gave it.

allOf.description: warehouses only on an S2 case, and never beside databases (Phase 3 design choice 1).
An S2 case names the warehouse legs it runs on.

status.description: acceptance: gating; diagnostic: run and reported, gating nothing (design, Merge rules).

databases.description: The databases the case runs on, when not all three (design choice 2, KO2-19): absent, it runs on DuckDB, SQLite and Postgres. Only beside exclusion, the owner's approval for leaving the others out, and leaving at least one out.

exclusion.description: The decision row (KO<phase>-<n>) whose owner approval lets databases leave a database out; only beside databases.

warehouses.description: The warehouse legs an S2 case runs on, and only there (Phase 3 design choice 1): at least one, none twice. Only on an S2 case, which must name them, and never beside databases. A case without it runs on the databases, and an S1 case without databases on every warehouse leg as well (run_python.py's case_legs).

paths.description: The scope-python.yaml paths this case covers.

routes.description: The paths python-core forces onto the core through SDM_CORE_ROUTES: every path the call may end on, since one call runs its paths on one route.

base.description: A base of contract/bases.yaml: DuckDB statements run on a fresh in-memory connection.

setup.description: DuckDB statements run after the base, on the same connection.

fail_call.description: The call the scripted endpoint fails, numbered from zero in the order the calls are received (T2.1a's serve(fail_call=), for main's multi-call predict, T2.8c): that call is answered 500 scripted_failure and every other by the rule; absent, no call fails. A JSON integer written as one, below 2**64.

probabilities.description: Whether the scripted endpoint answers a classification call asking for probabilities with them, as a model does (contract/runners/scripted_endpoint.py; T2.8's ranking cases, whose order is their probabilities): a JSON boolean; absent, the rule answers none.

quantiles.description: Whether the scripted endpoint answers a regression call asking for quantiles with them, as a model does (contract/runners/scripted_endpoint.py; T2.9's forecast cases): a JSON boolean; absent, the rule answers none.

outputs.description: The output fields SDMClient.predict asks for (its outputs=), passed as written (T2.9's quantile cases); absent, the call names none and the model's defaults for the task are asked.

explanation.description: Whether the scripted endpoint answers a call asking for an explanation with one, as a model explains the entity it is asked about (contract/runners/scripted_endpoint.py; T2.13's cases): a JSON boolean; absent, the rule answers none.

item_metadata.description: Whether the scripted endpoint gives each item it answers its metadata, as a model reports something of each answer (contract/runners/scripted_endpoint.py; T2.13's cases): a JSON boolean; absent, the rule gives none.

embeddings.description: Whether the scripted endpoint answers a call asking for embeddings with one on each item, as a model answers the vector it holds of each entity (contract/runners/scripted_endpoint.py; T2.11's cases): a JSON boolean; absent, the rule answers none.

view.description: The semantic model the case's source is (Phase 3 design choice 1): a Databricks metric view (metric_view, on the Databricks legs only) or a Snowflake semantic view (semantic_view, on the snowflake leg only), passed to the source's semantic_model by name with trust_expressions as written. With yaml, the view is created in the test schema from it before the run; without, it is an existing view, named by a placeholder the run resolves ({shop_metric_view}). Only on a case naming warehouses.

connect.description: The connect path the case's connection is opened through, handed to Schema.from_source as it is and found by detection (Phase 3 design choice 1): warehouse (sdm_connectors.databricks.warehouse(), databricks-sql), spark (a notebook's Spark session, databricks-spark), snowpark (a Snowpark session, snowflake) or lakebase (sdm_connectors.databricks.lakebase(), lakebase). The case's warehouses are exactly that leg.

until.description: The last public call the case makes when nothing refuses: Schema.from_source, then PredictiveQuery.materialize, then SDMClient.predict.

core.description: The core operations the call starts, with the inputs the host passes them. The pure-Rust host starts these; python-core records what its host passed and the comparator holds the two equal.

schema.description: The contract's QuerySchema; the query text is input.pql.

source.description: The contract's SourceSpec; the data are input.base and input.setup.

materialize.description: materialize's inputs beside the query text, which is input.pql. Not the schema it samples: that is the description describe_source answered, with input.edits made, which each host builds itself; a case naming one is refused (decision E50, the rust-host journey guard).

indices.description: The entities to predict for, one Arrow column: each a contract scalar of one integer or text type. None is a call the core refuses as the reference does (empty.indices, from T1.32d), so the host carries it.

anchor_time.description: The anchor time, a contract ts scalar, or null for the default.

seed.description: The sampling seed as the contract's signed hexadecimal text, or null for the default.

predict.description: predict's input beside its request state, which is materialize's answer handed back as the host held it, and its request id, which the host draws.

model.description: The model id the request is sent to.

from_source.description: Keyword arguments to Schema.from_source; absent means Schema.from_source(source).

relationships.description: Each a Relationship(source_table, source_column, target_table, target_column) passed in (T1.21b).

edits.description: Edits to the schema Schema.from_source returned, made in order before materialize (T1.21b): clear_time_column sets schema[table].time_column = None; delete_column runs del schema[table][column]; from T1.24b, set_primary_key sets schema[table].primary_key = column, set_time_column sets schema[table].time_column = column, set_stype sets schema[table][column].stype = stype, and set_relationships sets schema.relationships to a Relationship of each link. They finish describing the schema, so a refusal of one is the from_source stage's.

materialize.description: Keyword arguments to materialize: anchor_time is an ISO timestamp; indices_as decimal makes each index Decimal(text); inference_config is passed as written (T1.21b). An index is a JSON integer literal of any size, read without loss, or a string; both case loaders refuse a number written with a fraction or an exponent, 1.0 included, which JSON Schema alone would count as an integer.

anchor_time.description: An ISO timestamp, or the literal entity: each entity at its own time (T2.11).

context_anchor_time.description: The context's anchor time (T2.11), as anchor_time is written: an ISO timestamp, or the literal entity.

candidates.description: The rows a ranking is over (E153), each an entity key read as indices are: a JSON integer literal of any size or a string.

top_k.description: How many of the candidates a ranking or forecast answers, a JSON integer written as one; a value the reference refuses (0) is the case's input.

rows_per_call.description: How many entities one model call scores (main's 1fc5a686, T2.8c), passed as written: a JSON integer as an integer of any size, a number written with a fraction or an exponent as a float, true or false as a bool, a string as text, so a value the reference refuses is the case's input.

lag_timesteps.description: How many past steps of the target materialize adds as lagged features (T2.9), passed as written as rows_per_call is: a JSON integer as an integer of any size, a number written with a fraction or an exponent as a float, true or false as a bool, a string as text, so a value the reference refuses is the case's input.

random_seed.description: The sampling seed passed to materialize (T2.11), as written: any JSON value, a JSON integer as an integer of any size, null as None (an unseeded sample, a new one each call), so a value the reference refuses is the case's input; absent, the call's default seed.

num_hops.description: How many hops the sampler walks (T2.11), passed as written: any JSON value, null as None, so a value the reference refuses is the case's input.

num_neighbors.description: How many neighbours the sampler takes at each hop (T2.11), passed as written: any JSON value, a list as a list, null as None, so a value the reference refuses is the case's input.

max_pq_iterations.description: How many tries per example the sampler makes to find valid labels (T2.11), passed as written: any JSON value, null as None, so a value the reference refuses is the case's input.

use_prediction_time.description: Whether the model reads the prediction time as a feature (T2.11), passed as written: any JSON value, null as None, so a value the reference refuses is the case's input.

return_embeddings.description: Whether materialize asks for embeddings (T2.11), passed as written: any JSON value, null as None, so a value the reference refuses is the case's input.

exclude_cols_dict.description: The columns to leave out of the request, by table (T2.11), passed as written: any JSON value, an object as a dict and a list as a list, null as None, so a value the reference refuses is the case's input.

num_context_samples.description: The most context examples materialize takes (Phase 3's quickstart cases), passed as written as rows_per_call is: a JSON integer as an integer of any size, a number written with a fraction or an exponent as a float, true or false as a bool, a string as text, so a value the reference refuses is the case's input.

expect.description: The reference's outcome: where the call ended, and for a refusal the exception's class name and StructuredDataError.code (null for one without a code). message and today are for information only.
